newsitem.title: NORWAY: Nycomed says court rules in its favour.
newsitem.headline: Nycomed says court rules in its favour.

text.p: Norwegian pharmaceuticals group Nycomed ASA said on Friday that a court in The Hague had ruled against Bristol Myers-Squibb's claim of patent infringement against Yew Tree Pharmaceuticals, a company jointly owned by Nycomed and the Dutch OPG group.
"As a result, Yew Tree Pharmaceuticals will remain on the market with its new anti-cancer drug, Yewtaxan, in competition with Bristol Myers-Squibb's Taxol," a Nycomed statement said.
It said the ruling was made on Thursday.
"The active ingredient in both products is paclitaxel, which is known as one of the most effective drugs for the treatment of advanced breast and ovarian cancer," Nycomed said.
"Bristol Myers-Squibb had charged Yew Tree Pharmaceuticals with patent infringement, based on a recently granted BMS patent on an infusion schedule for paclitaxel.

"The court in The Hague found that this patent is probably invalid, and that therefore no sufficient grounds for an injunction exist. BMS has two weeks in which to decide whether to appeal the decision to the Dutch Court of Appeals." it said.

Yewtaxan, which has been developed by Yew Tree Pharmaceuticals, is the second paclitaxel product to reach the market. Up to now, the Taxol product from Bristol Myers-Squibb was the only available anti-cancer drug containing paclitaxel.

"This is the second time that Bristol Myers-Squibb has failed to stop the marketing of Yewtaxan. Earlier this year, the U.S. company filed suit against the Dutch Medicines Evaluation Board, requesting a suspension of the registration of Yewtaxan.
"The court in Utrecht rejected this claim. Later, the Dutch MEB, after a careful study of the Yewtaxan registration dossier, also upheld the registration," Nycomed said.
